headline: Prepare for banking sanctions and an 'alternative economy', including crypto bypass plans
dek: Netanyahu said Israel must prepare for the end of US military assistance worth tens of billions of dollars: 'If you think we're going to continue receiving what I secured twice, and that's tens of billions of dollars in American aid for the defense budget, prepare yourselves... because America has…
sources: Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu, interview with Israel's Channel 10 business broadcaster (TV10 Israel)
fault_line: Is Netanyahu admitting the US-Israel aid era is over -- or using a scare about Washington to win Tuesday's election?

sections.what_happened: Netanyahu said Israel must prepare for the end of US military assistance worth tens of billions of dollars: 'If you think we're going to continue receiving what I secured twice, and that's tens of billions of dollars in American aid for the defense budget, prepare yourselves... because America has changed... It's over, and it will end. It is only a matter of time.' He said he has ordered preparations for possible economic and banking sanctions, including an 'alternative economy' that can circumvent them, and that blockchain/crypto is 'one of' the options, with a plan already requested. He gave no date for an aid end and announced no formal US decision. Context cited by PressTV: a 2016 US agreement provides $38 billion over 10 years ending in 2028; a Chicago Council survey (Oct 5) found 56% of Americans want aid to Israel reduced or stopped.
sections.what_verified: Interview carried by multiple declared families: Haaretz, Times of Israel, L'Orient Today -- all reporting the same on-record quotes; aNews carries the same quotes (undeclared, not counted). Opposition leader Yair Lapid's response (aid will end + sanctions will devastate the economy if Netanyahu's government is re-elected) confirms the remarks landed politically.
sections.what_disputed: No US decision to end aid has been announced -- Netanyahu is forecasting, not reporting a decision; his framing ('America has changed, not Israel') is his own political argument days before an election. Lapid's reading (re-election = aid end) is opposition spin, not a US statement. The UK settlement sanctions last month are the cited trigger for the sanctions-preparation talk, not a US sanctions decision.
sections.why_matters: The Israeli prime minister himself is now telling Israelis to get used to life without American billions -- and to build a sanctions-proof economy to replace them. That is a rupture in the alliance story, whatever his election motive.
sections.context: Background: NEW to scans (big-missed; interview Fri Oct 23, recrawled Sat Oct 24) -- Netanyahu: end of US military aid to Israel 'only a matter of time'; prepare for banking sanctions and an 'alternative economy', including crypto bypass plans

totw_analysis: Our read: The Israeli prime minister himself is now telling Israelis to get used to life without American billions -- and to build a sanctions-proof economy to replace them. That is a rupture in the alliance story, whatever his election motive. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Is Netanyahu admitting the US-Israel aid era is over -- or using a scare about Washington to win Tuesday's election?
